description: Smart indoor bike dashboard on ESP32 2.8" ILI9341 display. Tracks cadence, speed, distance, BLE heart rate, Claude Code token spend, and HR zones — all on one screen. Reed switch sensor on IO35, Coospo H808S BLE HR strap, WiFi stats via local server, touchscreen HR zone settings.

userStories.title: Probe and identify bike signal
userStories.story: As a builder, I want to probe the 2-pin connector with a multimeter so I can determine the signal type (reed switch, hall effect, or other) and voltage levels.
acceptance: Document the signal type (digital pulse, analog, etc.)
Measure voltage range when pedaling vs idle
Determine if a pull-up or pull-down resistor is needed
Identify the pulse-per-revolution count (likely 1)
userStories.notes: Reed switch confirmed. 1 pulse per revolution. No polarity — either wire to either pin.

userStories.title: Identify available ESP32 GPIO pin
userStories.story: As a builder, I want to identify which GPIO pin on the ESP32-32E display board I can use for the bike sensor input, given that most pins are used by the display, touch, SD card, and other onboard peripherals.
acceptance: Map out all GPIO usage on the specific board
Confirm IO35 (input-only) or IO27 are available
Test the chosen pin with a simple digitalRead sketch
Document wiring plan
userStories.notes: IO35 (input-only) selected. 10K pull-up to 3.3V. Test script at firmware/test/test_reed_switch.cpp.

userStories.title: Wire bike sensor to ESP32
userStories.story: As a builder, I want to physically connect the bike's 2-pin connector to the ESP32 GPIO so the microcontroller can read pedal pulses.
acceptance: Solder or connect wires from 2-pin connector to ESP32 GPIO + GND
Add pull-up resistor if needed (10K typical for reed switch)
Verify clean signal with serial output (no excessive bounce)
Add basic debounce in software if needed
userStories.notes: Wiring: reed switch wire 1 → IO35, wire 2 → GND, 10K pull-up from IO35 to 3.3V.

userStories.title: Implement pulse counter firmware
userStories.story: As a rider, I want the ESP32 to count pulses from the bike sensor so it can calculate my pedaling cadence in real-time.
acceptance: Use hardware interrupt on the sensor GPIO pin
Count pulses and calculate RPM from pulse intervals
Handle edge cases: very slow pedaling, stopped, very fast pedaling
Debounce logic to avoid false counts from reed switch bounce
Serial output shows accurate RPM matching actual pedal speed
userStories.notes: Interrupt-driven pulse counter on IO35 with 50ms debounce, 3s timeout, RPM clamping (10-200), 4-sample rolling average.

userStories.title: Calculate speed and distance
userStories.story: As a rider, I want to see my estimated speed and total distance so I can track my workout progress.
acceptance: Convert RPM to speed using configurable wheel circumference
Accumulate distance over the session
Display in sensible units (km/h or mph, km or miles — configurable)
Handle the indoor-bike-to-road-equivalent conversion reasonably
userStories.notes: Speed from RPM via DISTANCE_PER_REV_M (6.3m). Configurable metric/imperial.

userStories.title: Set up Arduino CLI project and display Hello World
userStories.story: As a developer, I want a working arduino-cli build setup so firmware compiles and uploads to the ESP32-32E display board.
acceptance: Arduino sketch compiles with arduino-cli
TFT_eSPI configured for ILI9341 with correct SPI pin mapping
Uploads to the ESP32-32E display board
Basic 'Hello World' renders on the 2.8" screen
userStories.notes: TFT_eSPI configured for ESP32-32E (ILI9341_2_DRIVER, HSPI). Upload at 460800 baud (921600 fails).

userStories.title: Display dashboard UI v1
userStories.story: As a rider, I want to see a clean dashboard on the 2.8" screen showing my current RPM, speed, distance, and elapsed time so I can monitor my ride at a glance while pedaling.
acceptance: 240x320 layout with large, readable numbers
Shows: RPM (cadence), speed, distance, elapsed time
Updates in real-time (at least 2x per second for RPM)
Readable from typical bike riding position (~arm's length)
Dark background with high-contrast text for readability
userStories.notes: Compact portrait layout: RPM (font 6), speed/dist, time/HR, tokens/msgs, status bar. Dirty-region updates at 2Hz.

userStories.title: Auto-detect session start and stop
userStories.story: As a rider, I want the session to start automatically when I begin pedaling and stop after a period of inactivity, so I don't need to press any buttons.
acceptance: Session starts on first detected pulse
Session pauses after 30 seconds of no pulses
Session ends after 2 minutes of no pulses
Elapsed time only counts active pedaling time (excludes pauses)
Clear visual indicator of session state (active, paused, ended)
userStories.notes: State machine: READY → ACTIVE → PAUSED → ENDED. Color-coded status bar.

userStories.title: Log session data to SD card
userStories.story: As a rider, I want my session data saved to the SD card so I can review past rides and track progress over time.
acceptance: Session summary written to SD card as CSV on session end
Raw data logged every 1s during session
Summary includes duration, distance, avg/max RPM, avg/max speed
Graceful handling if SD card is missing or full
userStories.notes: SD on VSPI (CS=IO5). Files: session_NNNN.csv (raw + summary), summary_NNNN.csv. Auto-incrementing session numbers.

userStories.title: BLE heart rate test sketch
userStories.story: As a builder, I want a standalone BLE test sketch to verify communication with the Coospo H808S chest strap before integrating into the dashboard.
acceptance: Scan for BLE devices advertising HR Service (0x180D)
Connect to HR strap and subscribe to notifications
Print BPM to serial output
Auto-reconnect on disconnect
userStories.notes: NimBLE didn't work on this board (scan returns 0 devices). Switched to built-in ESP32 BLE. HR strap: '808S 0023713' at de:5c:38:c5:83:1d.

userStories.title: Integrate BLE HR into dashboard
userStories.story: As a rider, I want to see my heart rate on the dashboard from my BLE chest strap so I can monitor intensity while riding.
acceptance: BLE scan and connect runs in background
HR value updates on dashboard in real-time
Heart icon indicator shows connection status
Auto-reconnect on disconnect
userStories.notes: Built-in ESP32 BLE client. Notification callback updates volatile currentHR. Heart icon: red=connected, gray=disconnected.

userStories.title: Compact all-in-one display layout
userStories.story: As a rider, I want all metrics (RPM, speed, distance, time, HR, tokens) visible on one screen without scrolling.
acceptance: RPM, speed/distance, time/HR, tokens/msgs all fit on 240x320
Each metric is color-coded and readable
Status indicators for SD, BLE, WiFi in title bar
userStories.notes: RPM (font 6, cyan), speed/dist (font 4, green/yellow), time/HR (font 4, orange/red), tokens/msgs (font 4, magenta/cyan), status bar with rev count.

userStories.title: Add HR to SD card logging
userStories.story: As a rider, I want heart rate included in my session logs so I can analyze cardio data alongside ride metrics.
acceptance: heart_rate column in raw CSV data
avg_hr, max_hr, min_hr in session summary
HR=0 when strap not connected (doesn't skip logging)

userStories.title: WiFi setup with auto-reconnect
userStories.story: As a rider, I want the ESP32 to connect to WiFi so it can fetch Claude Code stats from my Mac.
acceptance: Connects to configured SSID at boot
Auto-reconnects if connection drops
WiFi icon on display shows connection status
Optional — dashboard works without WiFi
userStories.notes: WiFi STA mode, 10s timeout at boot, 30s reconnect interval. Green/gray WiFi icon in title bar. Credentials in config.h (gitignored).

userStories.title: Local stats server for Claude Code usage
userStories.story: As a builder, I want a local HTTP server on my Mac that serves Claude Code usage stats so the ESP32 can fetch them over WiFi.
acceptance: Python script reads ~/.claude/stats-cache.json
Serves today's tokens and messages on HTTP port 8888
ESP32 polls /stats endpoint every 30 seconds
userStories.notes: scripts/stats_server.py. Reads stats-cache.json, serves JSON with outputTokens and messages. Pivoted from Anthropic Admin API (tracks billing, not Max subscription).

userStories.title: Display Claude Code stats on dashboard
userStories.story: As a rider, I want to see how many tokens and messages Claude Code generated while I was pedaling.
acceptance: Session token delta with K/M suffix (e.g., '45.2K')
Message count during session
Grayed out when WiFi disconnected, '...' while loading
userStories.notes: Baseline recorded on first pedal. Delta updated every 30s poll. Tokens/msgs row below time/HR.

userStories.title: Combined session logging with stats
userStories.story: As a rider, I want tokens and messages logged in my session summaries so I can see coding productivity alongside fitness data.
acceptance: tokens_during_ride and msgs_during_ride in session summary CSV
Only logged when stats tracking is active
userStories.notes: Added to both session_NNNN.csv summary block and summary_NNNN.csv.

userStories.title: Touchscreen HR zone settings
userStories.story: As a rider, I want to set a target heart rate zone on the touchscreen so I can see at a glance whether I'm training at the right intensity.
acceptance: Tap HR block on dashboard opens settings page
Settings page with +/- buttons for upper and lower limits (5 bpm steps)
On/off toggle for zone indicator
Back button returns to dashboard
Limits: upper up to 220, lower down to 40, minimum 5 bpm gap
Settings persist across reboots (ESP32 NVS)
Zone indicator: green border when in zone, flashing red border when out
HR label shows zone range (e.g., '120-160') when enabled
HR zone range logged to SD card session summary
userStories.notes: XPT2046 touch via raw bit-bang SPI (MOSI=32, MISO=39, CLK=25, CS=33, IRQ=36). Interrupt-protected reads to avoid BLE/WiFi corruption. X axis inverted on this panel. Calibration: rawX 1770→0, 185→240, rawY 150→0, 1840→320. Preferences library for NVS. Dropped XPT2046_Bitbang library (SPIFFS calibration unreliable) in favor of direct SPI. Flash: 1866KB (94% of min_spiffs).
